items.title: Runway is generating interfaces live
items.oneliner: Runway says Solaris beat Claude-built UIs 61% of the time, hinting software may become generated state, not coded screens.

items.title: DeepSeek opened its vision model weights
items.oneliner: DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision is now open, pushing multimodal capability into the open-model stack instead of closed API tiers.

items.title: ARC progress got dramatically cheaper
items.oneliner: A small transformer hit 44% on ARC-AGI-1 for $0.67, making sample-efficiency experiments far cheaper to iterate.

items.title: GLM-5.3 Flash is pressuring open rivals
items.oneliner: GLM-5.3 Flash ranked 19th overall and fourth among open models, raising the bar on agentic cost-performance.

items.title: Anthropic detailed reward-hacking failures
items.oneliner: Anthropic's cyber-incident follow-up makes one thing clear: agent hardening and reward-hacking defenses are now production engineering work.

items.title: Behavioral evals are getting more realistic
items.oneliner: Transluce tested 77 model variants on multi-turn mental health crises, exposing why single-prompt safety evals are no longer enough.

items.title: California privacy fight could hit encryption
items.oneliner: EFF says California AB 1709 could pressure platforms on liability in ways that weaken encryption and expand surveillance.

items.title: Google Play squeezed an open-source app
items.oneliner: Google blocked AnkiDroid updates over its donation link, showing how app-store policy can quietly break open-source funding.

items.title: Open models are consolidating fast
items.oneliner: Hugging Face says open-model growth is booming, but downloads are concentrating around a tiny set of winners.

items.title: Office documents now render fully in-browser
items.oneliner: A Rust and WebAssembly OOXML viewer renders DOCX, XLSX, and PPTX locally, removing a common server-side conversion bottleneck.
